vcu_0159_0800ceb8.name: flash_lock
vcu_0159_0800ceb8.summary: Set FLASH.CTRL.OPLK to lock the flash program/erase controller
vcu_0159_0800ceb8.description: Read-modify-write of FLASH.CTRL (0x40022010, FLASH_REG_BASE+0x10) that sets bit 7 (OPLK) and leaves the other control bits unchanged. With OPLK set the controller refuses further erase and program operations until flash_unlock is called again. This is the Artery SDK flash_lock routine, written out as a single OR of the existing register value.

vcu_0159_0800cec8.name: flash_operation_status_get
vcu_0159_0800cec8.summary: Return the flash controller status: busy, program error, EPP error or done
vcu_0159_0800cec8.description: Reads FLASH.STS (0x4002200C) and checks the flags in priority order: OBF (bit 0) gives 0 = FLASH_OPERATE_BUSY, PRGMERR (bit 2) gives 1 = FLASH_PROGRAM_ERROR, EPPERR (bit 4) gives 2 = FLASH_EPP_ERROR, and if none is set the result is 3 = FLASH_OPERATE_DONE. The code returns 0 at once when the busy flag is set. This matches the Artery SDK flash_operation_status_get; the timeout code 4 is not produced here. Called after erase or program operations to wait for completion.

returns.description: flash_status_type: 0 busy, 1 program error, 2 EPP error, 3 operate done

vcu_0159_0800cf3c.name: flash_unlock
vcu_0159_0800cf3c.summary: Write the two flash unlock keys to FLASH.UNLOCK to enable erase and program
vcu_0159_0800cf3c.description: Writes key1 0x45670123 and then key2 0xCDEF89AB to FLASH.UNLOCK (0x40022004). The controller unlocks only when the keys arrive in that order with no other write in between. This is the Artery SDK flash_unlock routine. It must be called before any flash_sector_erase or program sequence, and flash_lock (vcu_0159_0800ceb8) re-locks.

vcu_0159_0800d06c.name: gpio_bits_reset
vcu_0159_0800d06c.summary: Drive the selected GPIO port pins low through the write-only CLR register
vcu_0159_0800d06c.description: Stores the pin mask into the port's CLR register at offset 0x14 of the GPIO block. Writing 1 to a CLR bit drives that pin low and writing 0 has no effect, so only the selected pins change and no read-modify-write is needed. This is the Artery SDK gpio_bits_reset. It has many callers across the application (vcu_0159_080022d4 and others).

params.name: param_2
params.description: pin bit mask, bit n selects pin n

vcu_0159_0800d070.name: gpio_bits_set
vcu_0159_0800d070.summary: Drive the selected GPIO port pins high through the write-only SCR register
vcu_0159_0800d070.description: Stores the pin mask into the port's SCR register at offset 0x10 of the GPIO block. Writing 1 to an SCR bit drives that pin high and writing 0 has no effect. This is the Artery SDK gpio_bits_set and is the counterpart of gpio_bits_reset (vcu_0159_0800d06c).

params.name: param_2
params.description: pin bit mask, bit n selects pin n

vcu_0159_0800d074.name: gpio_default_para_init
vcu_0159_0800d074.summary: Fill a gpio_init_type with defaults: all pins, input, push-pull, no pull, stronger drive
vcu_0159_0800d074.description: Sets the 8-byte init structure to the Artery SDK defaults: gpio_pins = 0xFFFF (all 16 pins), gpio_mode = GPIO_MODE_INPUT (0), gpio_out_type = push-pull (0), gpio_pull = GPIO_PULL_NONE (0x04) and gpio_drive_strength = GPIO_DRIVE_STRENGTH_STRONGER (1). Callers such as the GPIO setup in vcu_0159_08001ca8 overwrite the fields they need and then call gpio_init (vcu_0159_0800d0e8). Field layout: u32 pins at +0, then bytes out_type +4, pull +5, mode +6, drive +7.

vcu_0159_0800d08c.name: gpio_exint_line_config
vcu_0159_0800d08c.summary: Route a GPIO port pin to an EXINT line by writing its 4-bit port field in IOMUX.EXINTCn
vcu_0159_0800d08c.description: Splits the pin number into a register index (pin >> 2, selecting IOMUX.EXINTC1..EXINTC4) and a 4-bit field position ((pin & 3) * 4). It clears that field and writes the port source value into it, so EXINT line 'pin' is driven by port 'port' (0 = GPIOA, 1 = GPIOB, ...). Other lines keep their settings. This is the Artery SDK gpio_exint_line_config Its callers include vcu_0159_080020a4, vcu_0159_080021c4 and vcu_0159_080026f0.

vcu_0159_0800d0e8.name: gpio_init
vcu_0159_0800d0e8.summary: Configure the mode, pull and drive of the selected pins in CFGLR/CFGHR
vcu_0159_0800d0e8.description: Applies a gpio_init_type to the pins in its mask. Each pin owns a 4-bit nibble in CFGLR (pins 0..7) or CFGHR (pins 8..15), and the code writes the nibble from the structure: analog mode gives 0; input mode gives the pull field & 0xF (4 = floating) and also sets the output-data bit through SCR for GPIO_PULL_UP (0x18) or clears it through CLR for GPIO_PULL_DOWN (0x28); output and mux modes give (mode & 8) | (out_type & 4) | (drive & 3). The mask bits are walked one by one so untouched pins keep their configuration. This is the Artery SDK gpio_init. The structure layout is u32 pins at +0, out_type +4, pull +5, mode +6 and drive +7.

params.name: param_2
params.description: gpio_init_type: pins mask, output type, pull, mode and drive strength

vcu_0159_0800d0e8.notes: The decompiler shows the pull comparison against full byte values 0x18 and 0x28 (GPIO_PULL_UP and GPIO_PULL_DOWN in the SDK header).

vcu_0159_0800d18e.name: vcu_gpio_pins_all_high
vcu_0159_0800d18e.summary: Return 1 if every pin in the mask reads high on a GPIO port
vcu_0159_0800d18e.description: Computes (mask & ~IDT) == 0, where IDT is the port input data register at offset 0x08 of the GPIO block. The function therefore returns true only when all selected pins are high, and an empty mask gives true. Its callers pass single pins or pin pairs on GPIOA and GPIOB. It does not change any state.

returns.description: 1 when all masked pins read high, else 0

vcu_0159_0800d19c.name: gpio_pin_remap_config
vcu_0159_0800d19c.summary: Set or clear a bit field in an IOMUX remap register, encoded in one 32-bit code
vcu_0159_0800d19c.description: Decodes a remap code: the top byte selects the IOMUX register, bits 23..16 give the field's bit offset, bits 15..8 its width and bits 7..0 the value to write. It clears the field and, when new_state is non-zero, ORs in the value shifted to the field position, so a remap is turned on or off with one call. This is the Artery SDK gpio_pin_remap_config. Each call is a read-modify-write of one IOMUX register, so it is not atomic.

params.name: param_1
params.description: remap code: [31:24] IOMUX register index, [23:16] bit offset, [15:8] width, [7:0] value

params.name: param_2
params.description: confirm_state: non-zero enables the remap, zero disables it

vcu_0159_0800d32a.name: proto_session_bind_buffer
vcu_0159_0800d32a.summary: Bind a frame buffer and fragment size to a 36-byte protocol session slot
vcu_0159_0800d32a.description: Initialises one protocol session slot (0x24 bytes): stores the buffer pointer at +4, its capacity (u16) at +8, the fragment size (s16) at +0x14 and param_5 at +0x20, and sets the state byte at +2 to 1 (bound). It returns 0 and writes nothing if any of the buffer pointer, the fragment size or the session pointer is zero, because the fragment size is later used as a divisor. The init routine vcu_0159_0800cf54 calls it for five consecutive slots starting at 0x200022E0, each with a 300-byte buffer at 0x20002394. The field meanings are inferred from the callers and the size arithmetic, so the names are medium confidence.

params.name: param_2
params.description: fragment (packet) size in bytes, must be non-zero

params.name: param_5
params.description: stored at session +0x20 (passed as 0 by the init code)

returns.description: 1 when the slot was bound, 0 for invalid arguments

vcu_0159_0800d32a.notes: The +0x20 field is written but not interpreted in this function.

vcu_0159_0800d688.name: proto_session_build_frame
vcu_0159_0800d688.summary: Build a checksummed, fragmented frame for a protocol session into its buffer
vcu_0159_0800d688.description: Writes a frame into a session buffer: byte 0 = param_3, bytes 1..2 = param_6 and param_7, then the n payload bytes, then a 16-bit checksum (little-endian) equal to the ones' complement of the 16-bit sum of the three header bytes and the payload. It rejects a null buffer or payload, a payload over 0x6F9 (1785) bytes and a buffer smaller than n+5. On success it stores the state 3 at +2, the session bytes param_4 and param_5 at +0 and +1, the frame length n+5 (u16) at +0xC, clears the fragment counter at +0x1A and sets the fragment count at +0x1C to ceil(param_10 / fragment_size), with fragment_size the u16 at +0x14. Its caller vcu_0159_0800d2f6 first gets the session from proto_session_find_or_alloc (vcu_0159_0800a676) and then calls this function. The checksum is the same ones'-complement sum used by vcu_frame_checksum, so it is the protocol's frame check.

params.name: param_9
params.description: payload length in bytes, at most 0x6F9

params.name: param_10
params.description: total message length used to compute the fragment count

returns.description: 1 when the frame was built, 0 when a check failed

vcu_0159_0800d688.notes: Header byte meanings are not fixed by this code (the caller supplies them). The +0x1C fragment count and the +0x14 fragment size are inferred from the arithmetic and the caller that reads them.

vcu_0159_0800da38.name: util_load_u32_le
vcu_0159_0800da38.summary: Read a little-endian 32-bit value from a possibly unaligned byte buffer
vcu_0159_0800da38.description: Assembles four bytes at the given address into a u32 in little-endian order, using byte loads so there is no alignment requirement. The result is b0 | b1<<8 | b2<<16 | b3<<24. It is the read counterpart of util_store_u32_le (vcu_0159_0800dc54) and is a generic helper for multi-byte fields.

vcu_0159_0800da4e.name: vcu_can_ef00_frame_build
vcu_0159_0800da4e.summary: Build a 29-bit CAN frame for PGN 0xEF00 with three header bytes and up to 5 payload bytes
vcu_0159_0800da4e.description: Fills a CAN frame struct (word 0 = 29-bit ID, byte 4 = DLC, bytes 5..12 = data). The ID is priority << 26 | destination << 8 | source | 0x00EF0000 (PF = 0xEF, PGN 0xEF00 proprietary-A, PDU1 format), with the extended-ID bit 29 set and bit 31 preserved. The DLC is payload + 3, the three header bytes go to data bytes 0..2 and the payload follows. The call fails when priority is 8 or more, the payload is more than 5 bytes (so DLC stays at 8 or less) or a pointer is null. This group (vcu_can_*) builds the frames of the 0xEF00 proprietary channel, and the TP functions below build its multi-packet transport.
vcu_0159_0800da4e.notes: The header byte semantics are not known from this function alone.

vcu_0159_0800daac.name: vcu_can_tp_abort_frame_build
vcu_0159_0800daac.summary: Build a J1939 TP.CM connection-abort frame (0x18EC) for PGN 0xEF00
vcu_0159_0800daac.description: Builds an 8-byte TP.CM frame with ID 0x18EC (priority 6, PGN 0xEC00) from source and destination addresses. Data byte 0 = 0xFF (connection abort control), byte 1 = 0xFF (reason), bytes 2..4 = 0xFF reserved and bytes 5..7 = 00 EF 00, the PGN being aborted (0xEF00). It is presumably the abort sent when a multi-packet transfer on the 0xEF00 channel must stop. It is one of the TP.CM builders (vcu_can_tp_*) that share the same ID and data layout.

returns.description: 1 on success, 0 when the output pointer is null

vcu_0159_0800daac.notes: The reason byte is written as the fixed value 0xFF.

vcu_0159_0800daf0.name: vcu_can_tp_cts_frame_build
vcu_0159_0800daf0.summary: Build a J1939 TP.CM clear-to-send frame (0x11) for PGN 0xEF00
vcu_0159_0800daf0.description: Builds the TP.CM clear-to-send frame (ID 0x18EC): data byte 0 = 0x11, byte 1 = number of packets the receiver accepts now, byte 2 = next packet number expected, bytes 3..4 = 0xFF and bytes 5..7 = 00 EF 00 (PGN 0xEF00). The receiver sends it to start or resume a multi-packet transfer. Part of the TP.CM group with vcu_can_tp_abort_frame_build, vcu_can_tp_eom_ack_frame_build and vcu_can_tp_rts_frame_build.

returns.description: 1 on success, 0 when the output pointer is null

vcu_0159_0800db38.name: vcu_can_tp_eom_ack_frame_build
vcu_0159_0800db38.summary: Build a J1939 TP.CM end-of-message acknowledgment (0x13) for PGN 0xEF00
vcu_0159_0800db38.description: Builds the TP.CM end-of-message acknowledgment (ID 0x18EC): data byte 0 = 0x13, bytes 1..2 = total message size little-endian, byte 3 = number of packets ceil(size / 7) = (size + 6) / 7, byte 4 = 0xFF and bytes 5..7 = 00 EF 00 (PGN 0xEF00). The receiver sends it after the last data packet arrives. It is part of the TP.CM group (vcu_can_tp_*).

returns.description: 1 on success, 0 when the output pointer is null

vcu_0159_0800db88.name: vcu_can_tp_rts_frame_build
vcu_0159_0800db88.summary: Build a J1939 TP.CM request-to-send (0x10) for a multi-packet PGN 0xEF00 message
vcu_0159_0800db88.description: Builds the TP.CM request-to-send (ID 0x18EC): data byte 0 = 0x10, bytes 1..2 = total size little-endian, byte 3 = number of data packets (size + 6) / 7, byte 4 = 0xFF (no limit on packets per CTS) and bytes 5..7 = 00 EF 00 (PGN 0xEF00). It is only built when the size is more than 8 bytes, because a message of 8 bytes or fewer goes in a single frame. It is part of the TP.CM group (vcu_can_tp_*) that starts a transfer.

params.name: param_3
params.description: total message size in bytes, must be greater than 8

returns.description: 1 on success, 0 when the size is 8 or less or the output pointer is null

vcu_0159_0800dbdc.name: vcu_can_tp_dt_frame_build
vcu_0159_0800dbdc.summary: Build a J1939 TP.DT data frame (0x18EB) from a message offset that is a multiple of 7
vcu_0159_0800dbdc.description: Builds one TP.DT frame: ID 0x18EB (priority 6) from source and destination, data byte 0 = sequence number (offset / 7) + 1, computed as (offset + 6) / 7 + 1, followed by up to 7 payload bytes copied from the message. The offset must be a multiple of 7. The byte count comes from the in/out u16 *remaining (clamped to 7) and is written back. The remaining data bytes are filled with 0xFF. The decompiled index arithmetic looks off by one: the copy loop runs uVar2+1 times, and the padding loop starts one index too early, so the last copied byte is overwritten. The intended behaviour is 7 payload bytes per frame, so the exact byte count per frame should be checked against the binary. Its caller is vcu_0159_0800d34a, which advances the offset by 7 per frame.

params.name: param_3
params.description: byte offset of this chunk in the message, must be a multiple of 7

params.name: param_4
params.description: message source at the chunk offset

params.name: param_5
params.description: in/out u16: bytes remaining; clamped to 7 and written back

vcu_0159_0800dbdc.notes: Sequence number formula matches the TP.DT convention (1-based packet number). The byte-count and padding arithmetic is uncertain, see description.

vcu_0159_0800dc54.name: util_store_u32_le
vcu_0159_0800dc54.summary: Write a 32-bit value to four bytes in little-endian order
vcu_0159_0800dc54.description: Stores the low byte first, then bytes 1..3 of the value, into the four bytes at the destination. It has no alignment requirement and is the write counterpart of util_load_u32_le (vcu_0159_0800da38). It is used to fill multi-byte fields of outgoing frames.

vcu_0159_0800de48.name: nvic_irq_enable
vcu_0159_0800de48.summary: Set an interrupt's priority from the group setting and enable it in NVIC
vcu_0159_0800de48.description: Encodes the preemption and sub-priority values into one 4-bit priority with the current AIRCR.PRIGROUP setting (preemption bits = min(4, 7 - group), sub-priority bits = the rest), writes it into the top four bits of the priority byte and then enables the IRQ. For negative IRQ numbers (system exceptions) the byte is written to SCB.SHPR at 0xE000ED14; for device IRQs it goes into NVIC IPR at 0xE000E400 and the enable bit is set in the NVIC ISER word (write-1-to-enable, so the write does not disturb other IRQs). This is the Artery SDK nvic_irq_enable. The decompiled code writes the ISER register as a plain store, which is equivalent because the register ignores zero bits.

params.name: param_1
params.description: IRQ number; negative values select a system exception

vcu_0159_0800dec0.name: nvic_priority_group_config
vcu_0159_0800dec0.summary: Set the NVIC priority grouping (AIRCR.PRIGROUP) with the VECTKEY write
vcu_0159_0800dec0.description: Reads SCB.AIRCR, replaces PRIGROUP (bits 10..8) with the low three bits of the argument and writes 0x05FA in the VECTKEY field (bits 31..16) so the write is accepted. Changing the group after interrupts have been configured changes how existing priority values are split between preemption and sub-priority. This is the Artery SDK nvic_priority_group_config.

vcu_0159_0800e718.name: pwc_battery_powered_domain_access
vcu_0159_0800e718.summary: Enable or disable write access to the battery-powered domain (PWC.CTRL.BPWEN)
vcu_0159_0800e718.description: Sets or clears PWC.CTRL bit 8 (BPWEN) with a read-modify-write, leaving the other bits unchanged. While BPWEN is clear, writes to the RTC/ERTC backup registers and the LSE control are blocked. This is the Artery SDK pwc_battery_powered_domain_access and is called before ERTC setup.

params.name: param_1
params.description: confirm_state: non-zero enables access, zero disables it

vcu_0159_0800e728.name: pwc_deep_sleep_mode_enter
vcu_0159_0800e728.summary: Enter deep sleep with WFE or WFI, setting and clearing SCB.SCR.SLEEPDEEP
vcu_0159_0800e728.description: Sets SCB.SCR.SLEEPDEEP (bit 2) so the core sleeps in deep-sleep mode, then executes WFE (preceded by SEV, and twice so a pending event is cleared) when the argument is 1, or WFI when it is 0. Other values fall through with no sleep. SLEEPDEEP is cleared again after wake-up so later sleeps are ordinary sleep. This is the Artery SDK pwc_deep_sleep_mode_enter. Its caller is vcu_0159_0800688c.

params.name: param_1
params.description: 0 = enter with WFI, 1 = enter with WFE

vcu_0159_0800e754.name: pwc_voltage_regulate_set
vcu_0159_0800e754.summary: Select the voltage regulator mode through PWC.CTRL.VRSEL
vcu_0159_0800e754.description: Writes bit 0 of PWC.CTRL (VRSEL) to the low bit of the argument, keeping the other bits. The bit selects between the normal and the low-power voltage regulator. This is the Artery SDK pwc_voltage_regulate_set and its caller is vcu_0159_0800688c.

vcu_0159_0800e7b4.name: spi_default_para_init
vcu_0159_0800e7b4.summary: Fill a spi_init_type with the Artery SDK defaults (slave, full duplex, 8-bit, software CS)
vcu_0159_0800e7b4.description: Sets the 8-byte SPI init structure to the SDK defaults: transmission_mode = full duplex (0), master_slave_mode = slave (0), mclk_freq_division = DIV_2 (0), first_bit = MSB (0), frame_bit_num = 8-bit (0), clock_polarity = low (0), clock_phase = first edge (0) and cs_mode_selection = software (1). This is the Artery SDK spi_default_para_init, and the callers overwrite the fields they need before calling spi_init (vcu_0159_0800e7d4).

vcu_0159_0800e7ca.name: spi_enable
vcu_0159_0800e7ca.summary: Enable or disable the SPI peripheral through SPI.CTRL1.SPIEN (bit 6)
vcu_0159_0800e7ca.description: Read-modify-write of the first control register that sets or clears bit 6 (SPIEN) and leaves the other bits unchanged. It is normally called after spi_init to start the SPI. This is the Artery SDK spi_enable.

vcu_0159_0800e7d4.name: spi_init
vcu_0159_0800e7d4.summary: Program SPI.CTRL1/CTRL2 and I2SCTRL from an spi_init_type (mode, clock, frame, CS)
vcu_0159_0800e7d4.description: Applies the SPI init structure with read-modify-write of the control registers: I2SCTRL.I2SMSEL is cleared (SPI mode, not I2S); the transmission mode goes to SLBEN (bit 15), SLBTD (bit 14) and ORA (bit 10) for full duplex, RX-only, half-duplex RX or half-duplex TX; SWCSEN (bit 9) takes the CS mode, and SWCSIL (bit 8) is set for master with software CS; MSTEN (bit 2) takes master/slave; the baud divisor goes to MDIV_L (CTRL1 bits 5..3) and MDIV_H (CTRL2 bit 8) when the divisor is above 7; LTF (bit 7) selects LSB first; FBN (bit 11) selects 16-bit frames; CLKPOL (bit 1) and CLKPHA (bit 0) set the clock idle level and sampling edge. This is the Artery SDK spi_init. The bit positions were checked against the SDK struct.

params.name: param_2
params.description: spi_init_type: transmission mode, master/slave, divisor, bit order, frame size, clock polarity, phase, CS mode

vcu_0159_0800ea74.name: systick_clock_source_config
vcu_0159_0800ea74.summary: Select the SysTick clock source: core clock (no divide) or core clock / 8
vcu_0159_0800ea74.description: Sets SysTick.CTRL bit 2 (CLKSOURCE) when the argument is SYSTICK_CLOCK_SOURCE_AHBCLK_NODIV (4) and clears it for any other value, which selects the AHB clock divided by 8. This is the Artery SDK systick_clock_source_config Its caller is vcu_0159_08002030.

params.name: param_1
params.description: clock source: 4 = AHB without divider, 0 = AHB divided by 8

vcu_0159_0800ea90.name: vcu_systick_suspend
vcu_0159_0800ea90.summary: Save the SysTick enable bit to RAM and stop the SysTick counter
vcu_0159_0800ea90.description: Copies SysTick.CTRL bit 0 (ENABLE) into the RAM byte DAT_200018AC and then clears ENABLE. All three callers of the suspend, resume and deep-sleep routines list vcu_0159_0800688c, so this is most likely part of a sleep sequence (medium). vcu_systick_resume (vcu_0159_0800eab0) restores the saved state, and the pair forms a two-function suspend and resume group.

vcu_0159_0800eab0.name: vcu_systick_resume
vcu_0159_0800eab0.summary: Restore the SysTick enable bit from the value saved by vcu_systick_suspend
vcu_0159_0800eab0.description: ORs the saved byte DAT_200018AC into SysTick.CTRL, so the counter restarts only when it was enabled before vcu_systick_suspend. It never clears ENABLE, so a call without a prior suspend leaves the counter unchanged. This is the second half of the suspend and resume group.

vcu_0159_0800edb4.name: tmr_base_init
vcu_0159_0800edb4.summary: Set the timer period (PR) and prescaler (DIV) and force an update event
vcu_0159_0800edb4.description: Writes the period register at offset 0x2C and the prescaler register at 0x28 of the timer block, then sets SWEVT.OVFSWTR (bit 0 of offset 0x14), which generates an update event so the new values load into the shadow registers at once. This is the Artery SDK tmr_base_init. The timer must still be started with tmr_counter_enable.

vcu_0159_0800edc2.name: tmr_channel_value_set
vcu_0159_0800edc2.summary: Write a timer channel compare value (C1DT..C4DT) selected by channel number
vcu_0159_0800edc2.description: Stores the value into the capture/compare register of the chosen channel: 0 selects C1DT (offset 0x34), 2 selects C2DT (0x38), 4 selects C3DT (0x3C) and 6 selects C4DT (0x40). The codes are the TMR_SELECT_CHANNEL_n values, and the complementary variants (1, 3, 5) are not handled, so they do nothing. This is the Artery SDK tmr_channel_value_set.

params.name: param_2
params.description: channel code: 0 = channel 1, 2 = channel 2, 4 = channel 3, 6 = channel 4

vcu_0159_0800ede2.name: tmr_cnt_dir_set
vcu_0159_0800ede2.summary: Set the timer counting direction (CTRL1.CNT_DIR, bits 6..4)
vcu_0159_0800ede2.description: Writes the three-bit CNT_DIR field (bits 6..4 of CTRL1) to the low three bits of the argument, leaving the other control bits unchanged. The value selects up, down or center-aligned counting. This is the Artery SDK tmr_cnt_dir_set.

vcu_0159_0800edec.name: tmr_counter_enable
vcu_0159_0800edec.summary: Start or stop the timer counter through CTRL1.TMREN (bit 0)
vcu_0159_0800edec.description: Sets or clears bit 0 (TMREN) of CTRL1 with a read-modify-write that keeps the other bits. This is the Artery SDK tmr_counter_enable and it is the last step of timer start-up after tmr_base_init and the channel setup.

params.name: param_2
params.description: confirm_state: non-zero starts the counter, zero stops it

vcu_0159_0800edf6.name: tmr_flag_clear
vcu_0159_0800edf6.summary: Clear timer interrupt status flags by writing the inverted mask to ISTS
vcu_0159_0800edf6.description: Stores ~flag in the interrupt status register at offset 0x10. ISTS is rc_w0: a 0 written to a bit clears that flag, and a 1 leaves the flag unchanged, so only the bits in the mask are cleared. This is the Artery SDK tmr_flag_clear. Its callers are not visible in this packet.

params.name: param_2
params.description: mask of status flags to clear
